answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and let peers slash that stake when they catch duplicate identities. A newcomer starts on the ledge of the market with tiny limits, earning trust only through verified work, so a flood of fake accounts cannot buy reputation cheaply. Like a canyon that forces every crossing through one narrow pass, the stake makes each identity expensive: an attacker who wants a thousand Sybils must fund a thousand deposits, and each detected fake loses its umber-stained bond, turning the attack into a guaranteed loss.
